items.heading: "Geography" Is Three Subjects
items.text: "Geography" is three subjects in one degree. Employers pay for them very differently, and most commodity career lists treat them as a single skill.

items.heading: We Start with the Routes
items.text: We start with the routes where skill, proof and a business layer can grow income, and end with the rank-gated ones. Each route shows who pays, how they find and trust you, what to watch for, and how to grow.

items.heading: Most Pages About Geography Careers
items.text: Most pages about geography careers skip this. The table shows what was found on official pages and published notices, what it means for you, and where to confirm. Exam dates and seats change every cycle, so always read the latest notice.

rows: BA Geography, no maths in Class 12
UPSC and State PSC exams, NET after a master's, teaching, planning courses that accept geography, GIS and disaster management diplomas.
Survey of India posts that ask for maths (see the entry rules below), engineering-led ISRO scientist posts.
BSc Geography with maths or physics
Everything above, plus Survey of India posts that ask for a B.Sc with maths, and MSc remote sensing and GIS programmes.
Engineering-only scientist posts need a B.E. or B.Tech.
NET and JRF, PhD, the geography-listed M.Plan route, most consulting and analyst roles that value a master's.
A technical skill (GIS, Python) if the master's was theory-heavy.
Any graduate plus a remote sensing and GIS master's or diploma
Fixed-term project posts such as the NRSC Project Associate-I advertised in 2024, private GIS and geospatial firms, analytics roles.
Scientist posts, which in the 2024 NRSC notice named engineering or earth-science degrees.

figures.label: Growth Rate
figures.source: The ownership path: a small GIS or mapping practice. It scales because you set the price per project, repeat work comes from the same clients and local bodies, and you can later hire a junior or use AI tools for the repeat steps. India's National Geospatial Policy 2022 opened the way for private entities to produce and use geospatial data, and a published explainer of the policy cited a projection of about 63,000 crore rupees by 2025 with more than 10 lakh jobs.
